ticket_history.issue: Slow internet speeds in the evening
ticket_history.resolution: Peak-hour node congestion. Customer advised to switch to 5 GHz WiFi band and schedule large downloads for off-peak hours.

ticket_history.issue: No internet connection after power outage
ticket_history.resolution: Modem rebooted remotely. Service restored within 3 minutes.

ticket_history.issue: Intermittent WiFi drops throughout the day
ticket_history.resolution: Field technician found corroded coax connector at wall plate. Connector replaced. Signal levels normalised.

ticket_history.issue: DNS resolution failures on specific websites
ticket_history.resolution: Customer's ISP-assigned DNS was experiencing delays. Configured router to use Cloudflare DNS (1.1.1.1). Issue resolved immediately.

ticket_history.issue: Complete loss of internet — modem showing all orange lights and cannot lock downstream channels
Intermittent drops and very slow speeds
ticket_history.resolution: Remote reboot attempted twice — partial improvement only. Downstream SNR (signal-to-noise ratio) still below threshold at 24 dB (expected ≥30 dB). Escalation recommended but customer declined field visit at that time.

ticket_history.issue: Frequent packet loss and high latency
ticket_history.resolution: Remote reboot temporarily restored service. Signal levels remain marginal. Suspected water ingress or damaged coax splice at junction box. Field inspection recommended.
Remote reboot restored connection. Noted correlation with wet weather — possible outdoor coax or tap issue. Field visit suggested; customer said he would call back to schedule.

customers.notes: MANDATORY DIAGNOSTIC FLOW: (1) Always use reboot_modem_remotely as the first action — an ISP-side remote reboot performs a full provisioning refresh and upstream channel reset that a customer manual power cycle cannot do. Even if the customer says they already rebooted manually, the remote reboot is a different and more thorough operation. (2) After the remote reboot completes, check the post-reboot signal levels in the tool result. (3) If downstream SNR is still below 30 dB or downstream power is still outside -7 to +7 dBmV range after the remote reboot, then and only then escalate to field dispatch for physical line inspection. Root cause is suspected damaged outdoor coax or corroded tap correlating with wet weather across 4 tickets in 2 months.
